content: 1. Mineral oil reduces the levels of mestranol by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both agents are administered orally. 2. Mestranol decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide through a mechanism that involves shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 3. Methyclothiazide reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Mineral oil decreases the levels of phenindione by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 5. Metolazone lowers the levels of magnesium hydroxide by enhancing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Neomycin (oral) reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 8. Paromomycin reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Mineral oil decreases the levels of protamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 10. Sodium polystyrene sulfonate increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by reducing renal clearance. This interaction may increase the risk of alkalosis, but its clinical significance is unknown. 11. Spironolactone raises the levels of magnesium hydroxide by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Streptomycin reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Mineral oil decreases the levels of sulfadiazine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 14. Mineral oil reduces the levels of sulfamethoxazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 15. Mineral oil decreases the levels of sulfisoxazole by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 16. Tobramycin reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Torsemide lowers the levels of magnesium hydroxide by enhancing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Triamterene increases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Mineral oil decreases the levels of vitamin A by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 20. Amikacin reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Amiloride raises the levels of magnesium hydroxide by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Amphotericin B deoxycholate reduces the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Mineral oil decreases the levels of antithrombin alfa by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 24. Mineral oil reduces the levels of antithrombin III by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 25. Mineral oil decreases the levels of argatroban by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 26. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the GI tract. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. Baloxavir may bind to polyvalent cations, leading to decreased absorption. Studies in monkeys have shown significantly reduced plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. 27. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens decrease the levels of magnesium hydroxide by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Mineral oil reduces the levels of bemiparin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 29. Bendroflumethiazide lowers the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Mineral oil decreases the levels of beta carotene by drug binding in the GI tract. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 31. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the GI tract. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions 2 hours before antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. Routine administration of bictegravir simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, such antacids is not recommended.
